papers.title_en: Building a Nested LADDER for LLM Unstructured Post-Training Pruning
papers.authors: Nicolás Mauricio Cuadrado Ávila, Ivo Gollini Navarrete, Martin Takáč, Samuel Horváth
papers.evidence: 面向大模型的后训练非结构化剪枝与逐层稀疏分配
papers.tldr: 大语言模型训练后剪枝在高稀疏度下易出现质量骤降，非均匀分配虽有效但仍需控制退化。LADDER按层逐步增加稀疏度，每步评估额外剪除各层一部分权重的端到端损伤，并选择每移除参数损伤最小的层更新，从而生成非均匀且跨预算严格嵌套的掩码。在OPT、Llama、Qwen五个模型10%–90%稀疏度上，LADDER在低稀疏度与基线相当，70%后明显更稳健。该优势在多数模型的后验蒸馏后仍保留，并提升零样本准确率保持。
papers.abstract_en: Non-uniform allocation can improve post-training pruning of large language models, yet quality can still degrade sharply at high sparsity. To control degradation as sparsity increases, we introduce LADDER (Layer-Wise Allocation via Damage-Driven Evaluation and Refinement), which allocates sparsity incrementally. At each step, it evaluates pruning an additional fraction of weights from each eligible layer and commits the layer update that causes the least end-to-end degradation per removed parameter. This process produces non-uniform sparsity profiles and exactly nested masks across multiple budgets. We evaluate LADDER on five OPT, Llama, and Qwen models across 10-90% sparsity, using SparseGPT as its candidate-generation backend and comparing against uniform and adaptive allocation baselines. Results reveal a clear operating-regime trade-off: LADDER is comparable or slightly weaker at benign sparsity but becomes substantially more robust from 70% onward. This high-sparsity advantage largely persists after posterior distillation across four of five models and translates into improved retention of aggregate zero-shot accuracy.
